mechanism_narrative: A quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals strengthening economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters with GDPC1 growth > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns during periods of FEDFUNDS < 0.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 7%, labor market tightness leads to increased wage pressures, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE first falls below 7%.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between increasing housing starts (HOUST) and rising retail sales (RSAFS) signals broadening economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint HOUST and RSAFS growth does not correlate with significantly higher 20-day SPX returns (Pearson's r < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in two consecutive months signals supply chain disruptions, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following a 2-month INDPRO decline > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.5% during an economic expansion signals impending monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns following FEDFUNDS increases above 1.5% are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 6%) and increasing payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, but only during economic expansions.
failure_condition: Joint condition of UNRATE < 6% and PAYEMS growth does not correlate with significantly higher 5-day SPX returns during expansions (Pearson's r < 0.25).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in one month signals inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only when the economy is in a late-cycle phase.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of late-cycle instances following a 1-month CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5%.
